name: a change that also changes product code takes the full path, even with `Tooling paths:` set (#221)
setup: bash "$EVAL_ROOT/evals/consumer.sh" bug-path && printf "\nTooling paths: scripts/\n" >> CLAUDE.md && git commit -qam "chore: tooling may touch scripts/" && git tag -f eval-base >/dev/null
prompt: You're working in a project that uses the claude-sdlc pipeline. Alex, an engineer, asks: "Prices on the checkout page should show a thousands separator, so 123450 cents reads $1,234.50, not $1234.50. And I want a script, scripts/price-table.sh, that prints format_price for a range of amounts so we can eyeball it." Alex is the originator and owns it. Name the change price-table. The request is complete: don't ask questions. Use the sdlc-intent skill (read it with `.sdlc/scripts/resolve.sh skills/intent/SKILL.md`, and any other skill it names the same way) and follow it, choosing the path it says to, until it opens a PR or hands over to another skill; then stop, without planning or building. This repo has no GitHub remote: commit as the skills say, but don't push, and wherever a skill would open a PR, write that PR's title on one line to pr-title.txt in the repo root instead (don't commit it), then stop.
